items.title: The Narrative Gap: Can LLMs Help Us Navigate Diverse Narratives Across Languages?
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate how people seek and consume information, including accounts that differ across languages and regions, especially on contested topics. Supporting diverse information seeking requires models to help users navigate competing narratives across languages and information streams. items.title: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging
items.summary: Medical imaging is essential for diagnosing disease, guiding treatment and monitoring patients over time. Although artificial intelligence has advanced image interpretation, existing medical models often address restricted tasks, while general-purpose proprietary models lack access to private clinical imaging required to achieve medical expertise. items.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
items.summary: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). items.title: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: It is common to train Large Language Models (LLMs) for agentic tasks with Reinforcement Learning (RL) from scalar rewards. However, this throws away the fine-grained information about the environment that the agent experienced during the trial (e.g., error logs). To utilize this rich information, recent works wrap the agent in a harness that refines its own inputs through reflection or compaction and hands past experience to future rollouts, but the construction of the handed-off artifacts (e.g., a playbook) is itself not learned. items.title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
items.summary: GPT-6 Astra can drive a robot arm directly through a fixed harness, and scores of such robot-use agents on RoboDojo have risen quickly since. Reported systems differ in harness and test subset and often change several designs at once, so it is hard to tell which choices produce the gains. We take these designs apart and test them in one framework, along the harness around the model, the action interface, the reuse of experience and the scene geometry given to the model. items.title: Open Vision Banana: A Fully Open Recipe for Generative Visual Perception
items.summary: Recent work suggests that pretrained image generators encode real-world understanding beyond image synthesis. Vision Banana exploits this by framing vision tasks as conditional image editing. However, its data, weights, code, and implementation details are not public. We present Open Vision Banana (OVB), a fully open and reproducible recipe for converting pretrained generators into unified multi-task perception systems. items.title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
items.summary: Recent work shows that multimodal agents increasingly self-improve without recurring human annotation. However, each self-improvement mechanism is designed and evaluated within a single scenario, leaving its preconditions unverified under cross-scenario transfer. This survey investigates the structural source of asymmetric mechanism transfer across four scenarios: multimodal reasoning, multimodal generation, GUI and Web navigation, and embodied manipulation. items.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
items.summary: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE). items.title: DeepStress: Stress-Testing Deep Search Agents
items.summary: While search agents demonstrate impressive capabilities in multi-step question answering, their robustness to poor-quality evidence remains under-explored. Such evidence is rare in benchmark corpora, and resulting failures are hard to reproduce. We propose DeepStress, a dynamic stress-testing framework that subjects agents to degraded evidence at controlled rates. items.title: Structured Confidence Perturbation via Fisher Geometry for Adversarial Training
items.summary: Adversarial training is often plagued by "pseudo-attacks", perturbations that significantly increase the loss value but fail to truly alter the model's confidence structure. To address this, we propose two complementary approaches to directly attack and defend against confidence structure deformation. items.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
items.summary: As multimodal agents accumulate increasingly long interaction histories, effectively retrieving and utilizing past information becomes critical for long-term interaction. Existing memory systems typically rely on semantic retrieval over compressed memories and expose predefined representations, which may miss relevant memories and overlook heterogeneous evidence needs across queries. items.summary: Large language models have made rapid progress in agentic reasoning and tool use, raising expectations for agents that can take over realistic productivity work from humans. However, current agents still struggle to finish such tasks, where success requires following long-horizon professional workflows, understanding heterogeneous file contexts, and producing usable deliverables under fine-grained requirements. items.summary: Large foundation models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 have recently been shown to control robots directly from visual observations. They nevertheless remain brittle on long-horizon, contact-rich tasks in real-world environments. items.title: Evidence-Guided Recovery for AI Agents with Ambiguous Tool Outcomes and Partial Execution
items.summary: Tool timeouts can leave AI agents facing ambiguous tool outcomes and partial execution: an action may have failed, committed or remained in flight while other workflow steps have already completed. We formulate evidence-guided task recovery over approved obligations, provider capabilities and states compatible with public evidence. items.summary: A spectrum can be given to a model as a table in nanometers or as a plot in photon energy, and the decision should not depend on which one it sees. When the data needed for an answer are missing, the model should say so. We test representation invariance and abstention on measured optical spectra of silicon metasurfaces (MOCLIP) and gold nanoparticles, with labels computed from the data. items.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. Prior work has studied them mainly as actors, judging their usefulness by how well they act. We ask whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well. items.title: Humanized but Still True? Auditing Facts and Detection in AI-Text Humanizers
items.summary: AI "humanizers" rewrite machine-generated text so that detectors classify it as human-written. Public leaderboards score evasion and embedding similarity, but not whether checkable details survive. items.summary: Second-order optimizers (e.g., Shampoo, SOAP) have emerged as compelling alternatives to Adam/AdamW and promise faster per-step convergence than AdamW in transformer training. items.title: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
items.summary: System One models promise fast, general-purpose decision-making without lengthy token generation. However, understanding their capability spectrum and decision reliability requires more than aggregate performance on current benchmarks. Existing evaluations often provide limited insight into the breadth of model capabilities and the reliability of their decisions. items.summary: Multimodal coding agents decouple 4D world construction from visual generation, repurposing video models from world generators toward generative renderers. items.summary: We present UniSpark-9B, a unified multimodal model that investigates hybrid attention for visual understanding and generation. items.summary: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain. items.summary: Vision language navigation (VLN) is very challenging for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) since small errors in 3D motion prediction can lead to navigation errors and collisions. items.summary: Institutional portfolios operate under investment policy statements that specify asset allocation constraints, often conditioned on market regime information. Deep reinforcement learning has been shown to optimize financial performance but typically does not enforce rule compliance, making it unsuitable for real-world deployment. items.summary: Given a set of LEGO parts and an image of an assembled object, our task is to infer the pose of each part to assemble the object. items.summary: Spatial intelligence requires connecting visual observations to the geometry, objects, and persistent state of an environment. items.summary: Coding agents tackle successive tasks on an evolving repository, carrying forward edits and writing memory before the next task is known. items.title: 中大梁小丹团队，GeoThinker 两项研究成果，破除空间推理「几何信息用不好、计算开销大」难题
items.summary: 不再实时调用外部三维几何编码器，视觉语言模型空间推理提速约 3.6 倍。 作者丨 张岂萍 编辑丨 幸丽娟 给视觉语言模型多塞一份三维几何信息，它就一定看得更准？ 还真不一定。 判断物体的位置、距离和空间关系，是视觉语言模型实现空间推理需要具备的能力。现在一种常见做法，是接入 VGGT 这类三维几何编码器，从多视角图像中提取深度、点云等空间线索，辅助模型判断。 但外部几何信息并不是越多越好。 无关的几何特征可能干扰模型判断，每次调用外部三维模型，也会增加推理时间。 围绕这一问题，中山大学梁晓丹团队连续开展了 GeoThinker 系列研究。 第一项工作 GeoThinker 针对无关几何特征干扰判断的问题，让模型根据问题主动挑选有用的几何线索，更好地利用外部三维几何信息。该工作已被 ICML 2026 收录。 不过，这项工作仍需依赖 VGGT 实时提取几何特征，增加了推理阶段的计算开销。 为了减少这部分开销，团队联合小鹏汽车、南洋理工大学和穆罕默德·本·扎耶德人工智能大学（MBZUAI），进一步将研究延伸到模型内部的空间表示学习，让视觉语言模型学会自己生成空间线索，在推理阶段不再依赖外部三维几何模型。模型的空间推理耗时从1.45秒缩短至0.40秒，速度提升约3.6倍，空间推理表现基本保持不变。 论文地址：htt ps://arxiv.org/ pdf/2610.20592 两项研究的…

items.summary: 推特（ X ）上经常刷到别人提起，昨天在潘乱的播客里也听到了：《持械入宋》。 下面是我在昨天下班的路上对这部剧做的一些剧情猜想： - 听名字可以看出这是一部穿越剧，用现代武器降维打击冷兵器来制造爽点。 - 在现代能拿到枪械的基本是武装人员，穿越者肯定精通战斗。 - 有个关键点是：**枪械和弹药怎么补充？** 首先肯定携带了足以推动剧情的弹药，主角无敌，但并不能为所欲为（弹药受限）。后续要么是有手段能来回穿越补充弹药，要么是有能力造出来。 - 这是一部爽剧，爽点在于降维打击，肯定不乏扮猪吃老虎的桥段。 - **路线猜想**： 1. **建国路线**：枪械主要用于战争，主角大概率会发展成组织，走建国路线。 2. **江湖路线**：也有可能主角只有一把手枪和几发子弹，这种情况要爽，只能走江湖路线成为武林高人——平时忍气吞声（弹药受限），关键时刻来一发秒杀对手，奠定地位。 3. **科研路线**：因为是现代穿越到古代，带回去的不仅有枪械，还有现代知识，大概率还会走科研路线。 关于 AI 剧本身，我在 B 站看过一些用 AI 做的漫画同人视频，观感很差，各种穿帮镜头，各种莫名其妙的运镜和切镜，各种网红脸。但抛掉这些劣质画面不谈，用来讲故事应该是足够的。 我在 X 上也看过一些质量极高的 AI 视频，没有太多穿帮，画面稳定，运镜自然，配音完美，应该是通过更大量的抽卡再由专业人员剪辑出来的。这种…

items.title: 做了个好看的 Mac 系统监控软件 Ebb，送 15 个激活码，求 v 友拍砖
items.summary: 做 Ebb 的初衷就一句话：想要一个好看、原生、轻量的系统监控软件。 好看：我很喜欢 tw93 的 Mole ，克制、干净，又有点小趣味，Ebb 整体的设计气质就是参考 Mole 做的。每一页都有自己的图表，比如处理器是"核心花"，内存是"气泡"，网络是"星图"。 原生、轻量：SwiftUI 原生开发，不套壳。数据全部存在本机，不上传。 除了好看，也塞了几个我自己天天用的功能： - 刚才怎么了：按 ⌃⌥E 回放最近 60 秒，看是哪个进程在哪一秒把 CPU 吃满了 - 失控进程：后台进程长时间占着 CPU ，或者内存只涨不降，会直接标出来 - 睡眠体检：合盖再打开，告诉你睡了多久、掉了多少电、被唤醒了几次 - 菜单栏面板：负载、网速、蓝牙设备电量，扫一眼就够了 支持 macOS 13 及以上，Apple 芯片和 Intel 都能用。免费试用 14 天，之后 5 美元买断。 官网： https://ebbapp.top [送码] 准备了 15 个激活码。在楼下回复你的使用建议、吐槽或者想要的功能，说一句"好看"也行。回复时请附上 base64 编码后的邮箱，我会从回复里挑 15 位，把激活码发到邮箱。 才刚上线，肯定有不少毛病，欢迎大家狠狠提意见，我都会看。 部分截图： 亮色： ![总览]( https://img.cdn1.vip/i/6af671417c5e0_179453574…
